data.title: NexusMods Changes Hands
data.author: gmemstr
data.article_summary: Nexus Mods创始人宣布将日常管理交给新领导层，因长期压力和健康问题决定退居幕后。自2001年创立以来，Nexus Mods已成为他的整个成年生活，但他意识到自己精疲力竭，影响了团队和网站发展。经过多方寻找，他找到了理解和尊重模组社区的新 ownership 团队，确保网站的长期稳定和社区至上的价值观不变。创始人在必要时仍会参与指导，但不再负责日常事务，这有利于他和网站的未来发展。新团队包括Victor、Marinus和Nikolai，他们将引领Nexus Mods进入新时代。网站运营和社区支持将保持不变，继续支持模组社区的发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nexus Mods平台的优缺点及其在游戏模组社区中的作用

不同观点：
• [xnorswap] 认为Nexus Mods的体验相对较差，尤其是与其他具有内置模组浏览器的游戏（如Factorio）或社区自建的开源模组平台（如KSP的CKAN）相比。他希望更多开发者能提供更好的模组管理体验。
• [zeagle] 承认Nexus Mods在过去提供了重要的服务，尤其是在带宽昂贵时的集中存储库。但他对某些游戏（如Oblivion和Fallout New Vegas）的模组数量不足感到失望，并提到自己花费大量时间配置模组却没时间玩游戏。此外，他还提到Nexus在安全方面的表现（如数据泄露）。
• [orthoxerox] 批评Nexus Mods平台对某些模组的审查，认为它屏蔽了一些仅对字符串或标志纹理做轻微修改的模组，违背了分享模组的初衷。
• [brianjlogan] 对Nexus Mods持积极态度，认为它为像他这样的普通玩家提供了便捷的模组安装体验，尤其是在没有模组管理器的年代。他表示，尽管Nexus无法让所有人满意，但它对他的游戏体验有着重要影响。
• [strangescript] 对那些批评Nexus Mods尝试做模组合集的人表示不满，认为这些人对Nexus Mods有过高的控制欲和期望，而Nexus Mods作为一个免费平台已经提供了很多。
• [zelphirkalt] 认为Nexus平台的用户体验较差，注册和登录过程繁琐，希望未来能简化流程，让用户专注于下载模组本身。

补充讨论：
• Nexus Mods在过去提供了重要的服务，特别是在带宽昂贵时的集中存储库，但随着时间推移，用户对其体验的评价出现分歧。
• 争议的焦点包括平台对模组的审查、用户体验（如登录和注册过程）、以及平台在模组社区中的角色和控制。
• 一些用户对Nexus Mods的贡献表示感谢，而另一些用户则对其管理方式和用户体验感到不满。
• 安全问题也被提及，如数据泄露。

44296835.article_content:
After almost 24 years of running Nexus Mods, the time has come for me to step back from the day-to-day management of the site. This isn't a decision I've made lightly - far from it - but one I think is in both my and the community's best interests.
I started this project back in 2001, in my bedroom, with a 56k modem, an excitement for the upcoming release of Morrowind and with no grand ambitions or intentions. I didn’t set out to build a business, I just wanted to make a place where modders could share their work without worrying it would vanish into the internet either the next time a fansite went offline or a publisher decided they were done with it. That idea grew legs, sprouted arms, and turned into Nexus Mods.
Since then, this site has been my entire adult life. Every single day, for over two decades, I’ve been "on call", whether it was fixing issues, reading feedback, pushing updates, or getting pulled into the latest bit of community drama. It’s been rewarding, sometimes chaotic, often exhausting and always personal. Somewhere along the way, I forgot to step back and breathe, or sleep properly. The dilemma of running a major social network that does not rest!
The strain of being responsible for the behemoth I created has taken its toll. The stress of the job has been a regular source of anxiety and stress-related health issues. I realised that I have been burning out and this started to have an impact on my staff and Nexus Mods as a whole. So, I firmly believe that the best thing for the future of Nexus Mods is for me to step aside and bring in new leadership to steer the business forward with renewed energy to make Nexus Mods the modding community we all truly deserve.
One of the biggest reasons I've been doing this for so long is that I've never felt that I truly found someone who really "gets" the modding community the way I do. Finding a new owner who would be able to understand and respect the myriad intricacies of both Nexus Mods as a business and the wider modding community was essential.
After months of meetings, face-to-face talks, and a whole lot of soul searching, I am thrilled to say that I truly believe I have found the exact right people for the task.
So yes, the ownership of Nexus Mods has changed hands, but I want to be clear, this isn’t some corporate “exit” or a backroom deal. This is me doing something I probably should’ve done years ago: taking care of myself. Reclaiming some headspace. And finally letting go of the idea that I have to do everything and be responsible for everything myself.
What changes now?
Honestly, not a lot, at least not from your side of things.
Behind the scenes, I’ve already been stepping back bit by bit. Over the past few years, the team has taken on more of the weight and the site’s been doing better than ever. What’s changing now is simply the formality of it, making sure the right people are in place to guide Nexus Mods into the next era.
That includes some structural updates to the company ownership that we aren’t shouting about, but I want to be transparent: they’re about long-term stability, not changing the values or direction of the platform. Nexus Mods is community-first and mod-author focused, that’s not up for negotiation.
While I am stepping back, it's important to understand that Nexus Mods isn't just about me and hasn't been for a long time. The Nexus Mods you see today has been created by a team of 40 incredibly dedicated people, some of whom have been here for over 9 years. They live and breathe modding, they care deeply, they’re experienced, committed, and they're very much still here. None of that is changing.
So if I can ask one thing, it’s to continue supporting them, the site, and the community they help nurture every day.
In terms of new faces, you’ll also be seeing more of
Foledinho
(Victor),
Rapsak
(Marinus) and
Taagen
(Nikolai), who’ve come on board to lead this next chapter. They’ve got deep roots in gaming, tech, and most importantly, they give a damn; about the site, the community, and the future we’re trying to build here.
Editor's Note: We've added Nikolai to the new owners listed above. He works more in the background, but is still an important part of the team!
They have my complete trust, and I’m incredibly proud to be bringing them onboard.
What about me?
I’m not disappearing. I’ll still be annoying people on the Mod Author Discord, lurking on the forums, and sticking my nose into community matters when I can’t help myself. I’ll also be working with the team to help guide the overall direction of the site, just without needing to be the person who signs off on every little thing and without taking responsibility for any and all things Nexus Mods.
Frankly, that’s a good thing, for me, for the team, and for the future of Nexus Mods.
44296835.article_summary: Nexus Mods创始人宣布将日常管理交给新领导层，因长期压力和健康问题决定退居幕后。自2001年创立以来，Nexus Mods已成为他的整个成年生活，但他意识到自己精疲力竭，影响了团队和网站发展。经过多方寻找，他找到了理解和尊重模组社区的新 ownership 团队，确保网站的长期稳定和社区至上的价值观不变。创始人在必要时仍会参与指导，但不再负责日常事务，这有利于他和网站的未来发展。新团队包括Victor、Marinus和Nikolai，他们将引领Nexus Mods进入新时代。网站运营和社区支持将保持不变，继续支持模组社区的发展。

data.title: Google aims to reinvent email with Wave (2009)
data.author: xattt
data.article_summary: Google于2009年宣布推出Wave，旨在重新发明21世纪的电子邮件。Wave结合了电子邮件、即时通讯、博客、维基和公告板的功能，提供一种全新的沟通方式。与传统电子邮件不同，Wave支持实时编辑和多人同时在线修改内容，每个按键输入都即时可见，加快了交流速度。Wave还支持文件拖放添加、历史回放功能，以及将整个对话嵌入博客或网页中。此外，开发者可以编写扩展应用，如在Wave中进行国际象棋或数独游戏。Wave的自然语言处理功能还提供了创新的拼写检查。尽管Wave试图整合多种工具，但其核心目标是简化协作和沟通。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Wave的成败原因及功能分析

不同观点：
• Wave是一个超前于时代的产品，用户当时无法理解其价值。即使在多年后，人们仍然难以准确分类Wave，有人称其为社交网络、邮件终结者或聊天应用，但实际上它是一个原生的实时协作平台。（[xnx]）
• Wave的邀请机制和供应不足导致其难以在用户中广泛推广，特别是在教育环境中，这成为了一个严重的限制。（[angry_moose]）
• Wave的设计过于复杂，尤其是其实时编辑和显示输入过程的功能，让一些用户感到不适，特别是那些习惯于编辑信息后再发送的用户。（[hbn]）
• Wave失败的一个主要原因是缺乏承诺的功能（如将Wave嵌入网页），并且在发布后几乎没有更新，导致用户无法充分利用其潜力。（[Apreche]）
• 一些用户非常欣赏Wave的实时互动功能，认为这种即时性和协作性在其他应用中难以找到。（[jap], [tzury], [jdmg94], [thendrill]）

补充讨论：
• Wave在个人和团队项目管理中展现了巨大的潜力，甚至有人基于Wave构建了项目管理系统，但Google过早地放弃了该项目。（[tzury], [mark_l_watson]）
• 一些用户对Wave的消亡表示遗憾，并指出即使在开源后，也难以让朋友和家人使用它。（[mark_l_watson]）
• 有评论认为Google当时过于追求立即成功，如果以同样的态度对待现在的LLM（大语言模型），Google可能会错失领先机会。（[strangescript]）
• 对于没有使用过Wave的用户来说，他们好奇Wave提供了哪些当前产品仍未实现的功能。（[esafak]）

争议焦点：
• Wave的实时编辑和显示输入过程的功能被一部分用户赞赏，认为增加了互动性，但另一部分用户则认为这让他们感到不适和压力。（[jap], [hbn]）
• Wave的复杂性和超前性是否是其失败的主要原因存在不同看法，一部分用户认为如果Google持续更新和迭代，Wave有可能成功。（[Apreche], [strangescript]）

44298081.article_content:
Canada
How Google aims to reinvent email with Wave
Google wants to reinvent email for the 21st century. What's new in Wave?
Google wants to reinvent email for the 21st century. What's new in Wave?
John Bowman
·
CBC News
·
Posted: Jul 27, 2009 1:30 PM EDT | Last Updated: October 1, 2009
Social Sharing
Google Wave's inbox, as seen on the Official Google Blog.
((Courtesy Google))
In May, Google announced Wave, the company's attempt to reinvent internet communication. Brothers Lars and Jens Rasmussen, the Australian creators of Google Maps, have been working on the project for the last two years.
On Sept. 30, Google opened its preview of Wave beyond the 6,000 or so software developers who are currently helping to build the service. About 100,000 users can now see what Wave is all about.
Google Wave incorporates ideas from email, instant messaging, blogs, wikis and bulletin boards into a single new method of communicating. But we already have email, IM, wikis and the rest, so why do we need one tool that does all of these things? What is new in Google Wave?
How old is email?
The online tools you use every day might be older than you think. (Like everything on the internet, the date of origin of these tools is up for debate.)
Email/instant messaging: 1965
Bulletin Board Systems: 1978
Newsgroups: 1979
Internet: 1983
World Wide Web: 1989
Search engines: 1990
Web browsers: 1991
Wikis: 1995
VoIP: 1995
Blogs: 1997
Social networking sites: 1997
Microblogs (e.g. Twitter): 2006
Live editing by multiple users
In their first demo of Wave at the Google I/O conference, the project's lead engineer, Lars Rasmussen, and project manager Stephanie Hannon demonstrated how a conversation that starts out looking like an email, with replies going back and forth, can turn seamlessly into an instant messaging conversation if more than one person has the wave open at the same time.
Actually, the conversation is even more instant than instant messaging. Each key stroke by every participant in the wave is visible to all the others as it occurs. Rasmussen said this would result in faster communication than IM because you wouldn't be spending half the conversation waiting for the other person to hit "Enter."
However, he seemed to recognize that not everyone would want to communicate in this way, and said that a wave's settings could be changed so that messages are only sent after the user hits "Enter."
This live communication isn't limited to IM-type conversations. Anything in a wave can be edited by anyone who's been invited into it, including the original message. In the demo, colour-coded cursors, labelled with their owners' names, race around a document, all making changes simultaneously.
Playback
You can add people to a wave at any time, in much the same way you can forward an email. But someone coming into a wave after three other people have discussed and collaborated on a document might not see right away how the conversation went.
To address this, each wave has controls to move back and forth through time to see all the changes to the wave in the order they happened. Every wave stores the history of changes that have been made to it, in same the way a page on Wikipedia has a history, making the playback possible.
Drag-and-drop adding of files
Instead of attaching files as you would in an email, you can drag and drop files directly into a wave conversation. Google Wave's Stephanie Hannon showed how several people could contribute to a group photo album by dragging and dropping the files from the desktop into a wave. (She pointed out that HTML 5 doesn't yet support this function, and it required a browser plug-in called Gears to work.)
Dropping Word documents, spreadsheets or slide presentations into a wave could make collaborating on a project simpler than email, where tracking different versions of such documents can be challenging.
Embedding
A wave can be embedded on to a blog post (or any web page) in the same way a Google Map can. Changes made to the wave are immediately seen in the embedded version. In this way, a wave can act like a comments section on a blog post or a web-based chat room. A photo gallery created by you and your friends can be posted on your blog for everyone to see.
A sudoku game being played inside Google Wave. (Courtesy Google)
Extensions and applications
Developers can write their own applications that run inside Google Wave, in the same way that third-party applications run inside Facebook. In the demo, Wave's developers showed how a chess game would unfold inside a wave, complete with the playback feature to show each move in order.
A Sudoku game inside a wave becomes a competition to see who can fill in the most squares correctly. And because the team behind Wave also built Google Maps, they showed off a Maps gadget that allows two or more people to mark locations on the same map at the same time.

data.title: Insanity: Locked Out (2020)
data.author: theandrewbailey
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了一位极度忠实的谷歌粉丝，深陷谷歌生态系统，甚至搬进了谷歌打造的智能社区。在这个高度互联的“科技乌托邦”中，一切由传感器和人工智能控制，生活极其便利。然而，一次由于违反服务条款，他被系统锁定，无法进入自己的公寓，所有设备也失效。求助无门后，他试图用原始工具解决问题，但失败了。最终，他在愤怒中毁坏了社区设备，被警方逮捕，面临多项法律指控。文章讽刺了对科技巨头过度依赖的生活，以及在高度数字化社会中失去个人控制权的风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Google及其服务的可靠性存在质疑，特别是关于关键任务和客户支持的问题。

不同观点：
• **gloosx的观点**：不信任Google处理关键任务，强调需要有应急计划和备份。他分享了自己的负面体验：在Google Pixel手机上更改国家设置时遇到功能失效，且Google客服没有回复其支持请求。这表明他对Google服务的技术问题和客服支持非常不满。

• **gamegod的观点**：通过分享一篇关于Sidewalk Labs建筑的文章，似乎暗示Google或其相关项目（如Sidewalk Labs）在实际运营中遇到困难或失败。虽然没有明确表达立场，但通过分享文章引发对Google项目可持续性的质疑。

• **theamk的观点**：仅提到“Needs (2018)”，可能是在暗示2018年有类似的需求或问题未得到解决，或在指出Google服务的问题并非新近发生，而是一直存在。虽然没有详细说明，但可能是在呼应gloosx对Google长期存在问题的担忧。

补充讨论：
- **技术问题**：gloosx具体指出了Google Pixel手机中Play Store的“更改国家”功能失效，且没有错误提示，表明Google产品在技术实现上存在缺陷。
- **客户支持问题**：gloosx提到提交支持请求后未收到回复，显示出对Google客户服务的不满。
- **项目可持续性**：gamegod分享的Sidewalk Labs链接暗示Google的一些大型项目可能面临失败或质疑，进一步加剧了对Google可靠性的担忧。
- **历史问题**：theamk的评论暗示Google的问题可能并非新近发生，而是一直存在，提示用户需要长期保持警惕。

争议焦点：Google服务在处理关键任务时的可靠性以及其客户支持的有效性。

44297882.article_content:
Imagine that you're a loyal Google fanboy. You've had an Android phone in your pocket for as long as you can remember, and buy a new one every 8 months (at least). You believe that other search engines don't work. You died a bit when Buzz and Reader were killed, but you bought the rationale behind it. If a video isn't on YouTube, you don't watch it. You stood in line overnight for Google Glass, Google Home, and every Nexus device. You faithfully attend most Google conferences and product launches, live Plussing them on your Chromebook (to the annoyance of your friends), followed by an in-depth Blogger post. When you see a non-Google advertisement, or someone not using Chrome, you retreat to your brightly colored safe space.
When you heard that Google was building a neighborhood
, you remembered where you were. Your life changed. It felt like you found the promised land, and were the 937th person that immediately signed up to live there. You've drank so much of the kool-aid, you're almost swimming in it,
and now you want to live in a more physicalized bubble
.
Soon (a few years later), you move into the techno utopia
(beta version)
of your dreams. Sensors are embedded into every surface, to make sure things are "just right". Google's knowledge of you guarantees you will never see a non-Google or unrelevant ad again. You get served food that hits the spot every time. Since you work from home, shop from home, and all the "best" restaurants and venues are within walking distance, you don't need Maps anymore. Your cat eventually gets used to the self cleaning Nest litter box. Robotic trash cans sense that you're eating a candy bar while walking in the park, so one will open and follow you around like a puppy until you've finished your snack and given it a treat (the wrapper). You're living the best life possible!
But one day, you come back to your apartment. It's locked, and won't accept your authentication method.
Since your technocrat landlords despise plain old metal keys for some reason (What are you, a peasant?), they provide one of several alternative methods for you to open doors.
(Why can't those cyborgs be more like normal people?) They advise you to never share how or with what you use to login to them. Whatever it is, it's not working. You hope there's not an electrical outage somewhere: a friend had one of those happen to her and she almost died from the anxiety! (Someone across the room from her wasn't so lucky!) She's still going to therapy for it!
Because you're living in the future, everything is connected to the internet. Like most everything else, your door has a display mounted into it. A message appears, informing you that since you've violated the terms of service, your account has been terminated.
You're locked out from all your stuff!
There is a customer service robot downstairs, so you try to get some answers from it. Unsurprisingly, the robot is not helpful, not sympathetic,
and it won't listen to an unperson
.
You step outside and ponder why on Google's green Earth would you be locked out like this. It's probably something you said or typed, but you're not sure of exactly what. You're a good little fanboy, and every fiber of your being is progressive.
Maybe it was someone you knew.
Taking off your tinfoil hat, you figure that it's probably the local e-lord wanting to have some fun.
After living on the street for 15 minutes, you remember that a friend
sold hammers made out of roots
(or something) in the store. A few months ago, you heard of someone using one of those to get into his stuff. In desperation, you go to the store, but there's none there. You try to open a Hangout with that friend, but your phone is locked, too. It's very hard, but you remember where this guy hangs out in reality.
When you catch up to him, he said that he sold that side project to someone else months ago
, but Google eventually
stopped selling the hammer, because it didn't have a good enough description or pictures
.
While walking around town, considering your options, you pass by someone trying to give away her Google Home, but no one is biting,
because it's one of those big old ones
. She upgraded to the crumb-sized Home
Femto
. (So cute!) You gladly take the big one. You return to your former apartment building, and give that robot a piece of your mind. You relish both the robot and the Home asking you in identical soothing voices to stop. The cops arrive about 10 minutes later,
long after you've bashed both of them to pieces like they were fascists
, scratched your hands and arms in the process, and passed out at the sight of your own blood.
You were charged, not with something like trespassing or vandalism, but
under dozens of charges of the CFAA
, because
no one owns anything anymore
.
(You are merely licensed to use things, because you think that owning things is for chumps.)
You misused both the Home and the robot (2 charges), heard their requests to stop (9 more), failed to obey said requests (9 more)

data.article_summary: 2010年8月19日，志愿者在纽约布朗克斯为一个屋顶涂上具有高太阳反射率和红外发射率的特殊涂料。这种反光屋顶可以降低城市温度并节省能源，但暗色屋顶制造商正悄然游说阻止相关新规。2025年，田纳西州废除商用建筑必须使用反光屋顶的规定，共和党议员Rusty Grills称此举是为增加消费者选择。批评者警告，这将导致更高的能源成本和更多的热相关疾病。科学表明，浅色屋顶在炎热天气下温度比深色屋顶低50度以上，有助于减少能源使用和温室气体排放。至少八个州和十几个城市已采用反光屋顶要求，但行业团体质疑其科学依据，并反对全国统一标准。随着全球变暖，屋顶已成为气候战争的关键战场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：城市规划中的热上升气流及其环境影响，特别是对不同区域和人群的影响是否公平。

不同观点：
• 观点一：有人（如squircle）认为，虽然强热上升气流本身可能没有错，但需要证明这种由市场驱动的、自上而下的城市规划方式不会将熵（即无序和环境负担）转嫁给其他人或地区。评论者质疑当前的规划方式是否忽视了我们彼此之间的相互联系，以及这种规划对不同人群的影响是否公平。他们特别提到，不应让某些群体（如其他人的孩子）承受环境负担，而自己却置身事外。

• 观点二：隐含的对立观点可能是默认当前的城市规划和市场驱动的方式是可接受的，且没有显著的环境不公问题。虽然没有明确表述，但从squircle的评论中可以看出，他们反对这种立场，认为有必要质疑和检验当前的做法是否在环境和社会责任方面存在问题。

补充讨论：
• Squircle通过对比在阴凉公园和沥青停车场中的温度差异，指出了不同城市区域的热环境差异，这可能是由城市设计和材料选择导致的。评论者质疑是否有人研究并证明了这种设计不会对环境或某些群体造成不公。

• 评论还提到了生物区域主义（bioregional sense）的概念，这表明在城市规划中应更多考虑环境和生态因素，并质疑当前以市场为主导的规划是否忽视了这些因素。

争议焦点：当前市场驱动的城市规划是否在无形中加剧了环境不公，将某些负面影响（如热上升气流和环境负担）转嫁给特定区域或弱势群体，而受益者却不必承担相应后果。这涉及到环境正义和城市设计中的公平性问题。

Floodlight
Climate crisis
How the little-known ‘dark roof’ lobby may be making US cities hotter
As cities heat up, reflective roofs could lower energy bills and help the climate. But dark-roofing manufacturers are waging a quiet campaign to block new rules
This story is co-published with
Floodlight
Ames Alexander of Floodlight
Sun 1 Jun 2025 06.55 EDT
Last modified on Sun 1 Jun 2025 13.54 EDT
Share
It began with a lobbyist’s pitch.
The Tennessee representative Rusty Grills says the lobbyist proposed a simple idea: repeal the state’s requirement for reflective roofs on many commercial buildings.
In late March, Grills and his fellow lawmakers voted to eliminate the rule, scrapping a measure meant to save energy, lower temperatures and protect Tennesseans from extreme heat.
Grills, a Republican, told Floodlight that he introduced the bill to give consumers more choice.
It was another win for a well-organized lobbying campaign led by manufacturers of dark roofing materials.
Industry representatives called the rollback in Tennessee a needed correction as more of the state moved into a hotter climate zone, expanding the reach of the state’s cool-roof rule. Critics called it dangerous and “deceptive”.
“The new law will lead to higher energy costs and greater heat-related illnesses and deaths,” state representative Harold Love and the Rev Jon Robinson said in a statement.
It will, critics warned, make Nashville, Memphis and other cities hotter – particularly in underserved Black and Latino communities, where many struggle to pay their utility bills. Similar lobbying has played out in Denver and Baltimore and at the national level.
Industry groups have questioned the decades-old science behind cool roofs, downplayed the benefits and warned of reduced choice and unintended consequences. “A one-size-fits-all approach doesn’t consider climate variation across different regions,” wrote Ellen Thorp, the executive director of the EPDM Roofing Association, a DC-based national group that represents an industry built primarily on dark materials.
View image in fullscreen
Rusty Grills in Nashville in 2023.
Photograph: George Walker IV/AP
But the weight of the scientific evidence is clear: on hot days, light-colored roofs can stay more than 50 degrees cooler than dark ones, helping cut energy use, curb greenhouse gas emissions and reduce heat-related illnesses and deaths. One
recent study
found that reflective roofs could have saved the lives of more than 240 people who died in London’s 2018 heatwave.
At least eight states – and more than a dozen cities in other states – have adopted cool-roof requirements, according to the
Smart Surfaces Coalition
, a national group of public health and environmental groups that promote reflective roofs, trees and other solutions to make cities healthier.
Industry representatives lobbied successfully in recent months against expanding cool roof recommendations in national professional energy efficiency codes – the standards that many cities and states use to set building regulations.
The stakes are high. As global temperatures rise and heatwaves
grow more deadly
, roofs have become battlefields in a consequential climate war. It’s happening as the Trump administration and Congress
move to derail
measures designed to make appliances and buildings more energy efficient.
Why roof color matters
The principle is simple: light-colored roofs reflect sunlight, so buildings stay cooler. Dark ones absorb heat, driving up temperatures inside buildings and in the surrounding air.
Roofs comprise up to one-fourth of the surface area of major US cities, researchers say, so the color of roofs can make a big difference in urban areas.
Just how hot can dark roofs get?
“You can physically burn your hands on these roofs,” said Bill Updike, who used to install solar panels and now works for the Smart Surfaces Coalition.
Study after study has confirmed the benefits of light-colored roofs. They save energy, lower air-conditioning bills and reduce city temperatures. They help prevent heat-related illnesses. And they typically cost no more than dark roofs.
A
study
by the US Department of Energy’s Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory found that a cool roof on a home in central California saved 20% in annual energy costs.
View image in fullscreen
A researcher from the Berkeley lab perform tests on cooling materials.
Photograph: Thor Swift/Berkeley Lab
In a three-story rowhouse in Baltimore, Owen Henry discovered what a difference a cool roof can make.

data.title: Chemical knowledge and reasoning of large language models vs. chemist expertise
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为ChemBench的自动化框架，用于评估大型语言模型（LLMs）在化学知识和推理能力方面与化学专家的对比表现。研究收集了超过2,700个问答对，评估了多种开放和封闭源的LLMs，发现顶级模型在平均表现上优于人类化学家。然而，这些模型在处理某些基本任务时仍显不足，并且常常给出过于自信的预测。研究结果展示了LLMs在化学领域的强大潜力，但同时也强调了进一步研究以提高其安全性和实用性的必要性。此外，本文建议调整化学教育，并强调了在特定领域评估LLMs的基准框架的价值。最后，文章也关注了LLMs在化学安全方面的潜在风险和误用问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在化学及其他专业领域（如计算机科学、编程等）中的应用与局限

不同观点：
• PlasmonOwl（化学家的视角）：LLM在化学领域表现不佳，因为化学研究依赖于实践经验和直觉，而这些是LLM不具备的。化学家通过长期的研究积累直觉，而LLM只能处理表面的、记忆性的知识，无法胜任复杂的化学研究任务。例如，化学中的颜色变化可能意味着实验反应的成败，而LLM无法通过简单的提问理解这些细微的实验现象。

• calibas（计算机科学视角）：LLM在计算机科学领域表现优异，因为它们可以快速学习大量的知识，尽管这些知识的深度有限。LLM可以掌握许多编程语言，包括一些冷门的语言，但它们在专业领域上仍然难以超越专注于该领域的人类专家。

• 6LLvveMx2koXfwn（对同行评审制度的反思）：评论指出了同行评审期刊文章在快速发展领域中的局限性，暗示这种出版模式可能已经过时。

• pu_pe（对人类比较的质疑）：认为将LLM与仅有硕士学位的人类专家进行比较不公平，因为专家领域内的细分差异很大，类似于要求心脏病专家回答神经学问题是不合理的。

• sgt101（书籍与LLM的比较）：强调书籍作为知识来源的重要性，认为LLM可以作为一种超级互动索引系统来使用，帮助查找知识。

• gavinray（伦理与安全问题）：展示了LLM在化学合成路径设计中的潜力，但也提出了伦理和安全方面的担忧，例如可能被用于不当用途。

• marcodiego（模型改进的潜力）：指出LLM在回答知识密集型问题上的局限性，但同时也认为通过在更专业的数据源上进行训练，或者与专业数据库集成，LLM的性能可以进一步提升。

• AvAn12（人类贡献的质疑）：质疑LLM的成就可能依赖于人类专家的贡献，暗示这些模型可能只是整合了大量人类创建的内容。

• fuzzfactor（工业视角）：从工业应用的角度出发，认为LLM的学术讨论与实际工业需求脱节，强调实践经验的重要性。

补充讨论：
• LLM在不同专业领域中的表现各异，化学和计算机科学是两个典型的对比例子。
• LLM的知识广度与深度之间的矛盾是其在专业领域应用中的一大挑战。
• 对LLM在实际应用中的伦理和安全问题提出了担忧，尤其是在敏感领域如化学合成中的潜在不当使用。
• 对LLM模型未来改进的方向提出了建议，包括训练数据的选择和与专业数据库的集成。
• 强调了实践经验和直觉在某些专业领域中的不可替代性。

44275471.article_content:
A framework for evaluating the chemical knowledge and reasoning abilities of large language models against the expertise of chemists
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Chemical safety
Cheminformatics
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) have gained widespread interest owing to their ability to process human language and perform tasks on which they have not been explicitly trained. However, we possess only a limited systematic understanding of the chemical capabilities of LLMs, which would be required to improve models and mitigate potential harm. Here we introduce ChemBench, an automated framework for evaluating the chemical knowledge and reasoning abilities of state-of-the-art LLMs against the expertise of chemists. We curated more than 2,700 question–answer pairs, evaluated leading open- and closed-source LLMs and found that the best models, on average, outperformed the best human chemists in our study. However, the models struggle with some basic tasks and provide overconfident predictions. These findings reveal LLMs’ impressive chemical capabilities while emphasizing the need for further research to improve their safety and usefulness. They also suggest adapting chemistry education and show the value of benchmarking frameworks for evaluating LLMs in specific domains.

In addition, since a lot—if not most—of the information about chemistry is currently stored and communicated in text, there is a strong reason to believe that there is still a lot of untapped potential in LLMs for chemistry and materials science

44275471.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为ChemBench的自动化框架，用于评估大型语言模型（LLMs）在化学知识和推理能力方面与化学专家的对比表现。研究收集了超过2,700个问答对，评估了多种开放和封闭源的LLMs，发现顶级模型在平均表现上优于人类化学家。然而，这些模型在处理某些基本任务时仍显不足，并且常常给出过于自信的预测。研究结果展示了LLMs在化学领域的强大潜力，但同时也强调了进一步研究以提高其安全性和实用性的必要性。此外，本文建议调整化学教育，并强调了在特定领域评估LLMs的基准框架的价值。最后，文章也关注了LLMs在化学安全方面的潜在风险和误用问题。
44275471.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在化学及其他专业领域（如计算机科学、编程等）中的应用与局限

不同观点：
• PlasmonOwl（化学家的视角）：LLM在化学领域表现不佳，因为化学研究依赖于实践经验和直觉，而这些是LLM不具备的。化学家通过长期的研究积累直觉，而LLM只能处理表面的、记忆性的知识，无法胜任复杂的化学研究任务。例如，化学中的颜色变化可能意味着实验反应的成败，而LLM无法通过简单的提问理解这些细微的实验现象。

• calibas（计算机科学视角）：LLM在计算机科学领域表现优异，因为它们可以快速学习大量的知识，尽管这些知识的深度有限。LLM可以掌握许多编程语言，包括一些冷门的语言，但它们在专业领域上仍然难以超越专注于该领域的人类专家。

• 6LLvveMx2koXfwn（对同行评审制度的反思）：评论指出了同行评审期刊文章在快速发展领域中的局限性，暗示这种出版模式可能已经过时。

• pu_pe（对人类比较的质疑）：认为将LLM与仅有硕士学位的人类专家进行比较不公平，因为专家领域内的细分差异很大，类似于要求心脏病专家回答神经学问题是不合理的。

• sgt101（书籍与LLM的比较）：强调书籍作为知识来源的重要性，认为LLM可以作为一种超级互动索引系统来使用，帮助查找知识。

• gavinray（伦理与安全问题）：展示了LLM在化学合成路径设计中的潜力，但也提出了伦理和安全方面的担忧，例如可能被用于不当用途。

• marcodiego（模型改进的潜力）：指出LLM在回答知识密集型问题上的局限性，但同时也认为通过在更专业的数据源上进行训练，或者与专业数据库集成，LLM的性能可以进一步提升。

• AvAn12（人类贡献的质疑）：质疑LLM的成就可能依赖于人类专家的贡献，暗示这些模型可能只是整合了大量人类创建的内容。

• fuzzfactor（工业视角）：从工业应用的角度出发，认为LLM的学术讨论与实际工业需求脱节，强调实践经验的重要性。

补充讨论：
• LLM在不同专业领域中的表现各异，化学和计算机科学是两个典型的对比例子。
• LLM的知识广度与深度之间的矛盾是其在专业领域应用中的一大挑战。
• 对LLM在实际应用中的伦理和安全问题提出了担忧，尤其是在敏感领域如化学合成中的潜在不当使用。
• 对LLM模型未来改进的方向提出了建议，包括训练数据的选择和与专业数据库的集成。
• 强调了实践经验和直觉在某些专业领域中的不可替代性。

data.author: durakot
data.article_summary: 亚历山大·波波夫（Oleksandr Popov）1967年出生于基辅，父亲是计算机科学家，母亲是演员，这种科技与艺术的双重背景深刻影响了他的艺术视野。童年时常随父亲接触早期苏联计算机，并在母亲指导下学习表演。1975至1983年，他在基辅数学与计算机专科学校表现出色，14岁时制作了简易的互动“算命机”。1982年，发表关于早期聊天机器人概念的论文。1983年，入读明斯克理工学院，但对僵化的课程失望，转而加入地下计算机团体“Elektronika”，开发兼具游戏和心理实验性质的程序。1986年，与团体理念分歧后创立“PopovSoft Ltd”，开发多款实验性软件，包括引发心理效应的“Labirint Razuma”和24小时实验程序“Ispytaniye”。1988年，辍学投身行为艺术，结束PopovSoft Ltd。波波夫的创作始终探索技术与意识的本质。

44283239.article_content:
Alexander Popov — Biographical Timeline
“The experience continues until you stop experiencing it.”
1967
Born in Kyiv, Ukraine (then Ukrainian SSR) as Oleksandr Mykhailo Popov
. His father, Dr. Mikhail Popov, was a respected computer scientist at the
V.M. Glushkov Institute of Cybernetics
of the National Academy of Sciences (NAS) of Ukraine, working on early artificial intelligence systems and cybernetic theory. His mother, Lyudmila Popova (née Kovalenko), was a prominent actress with the Lesya Ukrainka National Academic Theater. This dual heritage of cutting-edge technology and theatrical performance would profoundly shape his artistic vision.
1970-1975
As a child, frequently accompanies his father to the Glushkov Institute, where he is exposed to the
MESM (Small Electronic Calculating Machine)
and other early Soviet computers. Institute colleagues recall a precocious boy who would ask sophisticated questions about machine logic and human-computer interaction. At home, his mother trains him in voice, movement, and dramatic presentation, treating their apartment as an informal theater studio.
1975-1983
Attends the specialized
School No. 145 for mathematics and computer science in Kyiv
, showing remarkable aptitude for both programming and electronics. Creates his first rudimentary interactive experience at age 14, combining a reprogrammed calculator, tape recorder, and homemade electronic circuits to create a “fortune-telling machine” that responded differently based on how users interacted with it. His teachers note his unusual interest in the psychological effects of human-computer interaction.
1982
While still in school, publishes a paper in a youth science journal detailing an algorithm for generating “conversational responses that create the illusion of understanding,” essentially an early chatbot concept. The paper includes philosophical questions about the nature of consciousness and reality that seem advanced for his age
1983
Following his father’s connections and recommendations, moves to Minsk to attend the prestigious
Belarusian Polytechnic Institute
(now Belarusian National Technical University) to study computer engineering. His professors initially have high expectations due to his father’s reputation in Soviet computing circles.
1984
Becomes increasingly disenchanted with the rigid technical curriculum. Finds an intellectual home in the underground “Elektronika” collective, a secret group of students and young engineers creating unofficial games and programs for Soviet computers like the
Elektronika BK-0010
and
MK-61 programmable calculators
. The group eventually acquires smuggled Commodore 64 systems through Polish connections, opening Alexander’s eyes to Western game design.
1985
While maintaining adequate academic performance, devotes increasing time to the Elektronika collective. Develops a reputation for creating programs that blur the line between games and psychological experiments. Creates “Dialog s Neznakomtsem” (Dialogue with a Stranger), a text-based program that asks increasingly personal questions and responds in ways designed to create emotional attachment to the computer.
1986
Has philosophical falling out with the Elektronika collective over the purpose of computing. While most members are interested in replicating Western gaming experiences, Popov argues for creating “new realities that question the nature of consciousness.” Leaves the group and establishes “PopovSoft Ltd,” an ironically named one-person “company” that becomes his publishing identity for increasingly experimental software.
1986-1987
Under the PopovSoft Ltd label, develops several boundary-pushing programs including “Kosmos-3” (a space simulation with philosophical elements) and his most significant early work, “Labirint Razuma” (Labyrinth of the Mind). This latter program combines mathematical puzzles with existential questions and was distributed on magnetic tapes throughout the Soviet computing underground. Users reported strange psychological effects after prolonged interaction with the program, establishing Popov’s early interest in altered states of consciousness through technology.
1987
Creates the controversial “Ispytaniye” (The Test), his most technically sophisticated program for the
Elektronika BK-0010
. Designed to run for exactly 24 hours, it requires participants to interact with it at specific intervals, tracking whether they are following instructions even when not at the computer. The few who completed the full cycle reported experiencing “a profound shift in perception.” Computer historians later note similarities between this work and his later physical installations.
1988
Abandons his studies at the Polytechnic Institute after becoming disillusioned with the rigid Soviet educational system. Begins experimenting with performance art, staging small happenings that combine technology and audience participation. 主要讨论点：关于“Unaware Adversaries”文章的评价与延伸讨论

不同观点：
• [ycombiredd] 认为自己并非学术背景，而是一个有丰富经验的IT从业者（系统/网络工程师，企业架构师）。他以一种半幽默、仿学术的风格撰写了一篇文章，最初是基于自己小学四年级时的一个趣闻。他对于文章的学术严谨性并不自信，但希望有人能阅读并产生兴趣。

• [troelsSteegin] 对文章表示欣赏，并提出了进一步的思考。他认为在将系统范围的信息提供给个体代理时，模型需要考虑代理的信息处理能力，比如注意力或分析预算。他进一步指出，信息的不对称性不仅仅在于信息的获取，还在于信息的解读。

补充讨论：
• [troelsSteegin] 提出了对信息处理能力的关注，强调了个体代理在面对大量信息时的分析和注意力限制。他认为这是信息不对称的一个重要方面，应该在模型中有所体现。

• [ycombiredd] 的文章核心基于一个实际趣闻，他以个人经历为起点，尝试用一种非传统的、幽默的方式探讨学术问题，表明他对于自己非学术背景的谦逊态度，但也显示出其对复杂主题的独特视角。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点可能在于学术讨论中非传统方法的有效性和认可度。例如，[ycombiredd] 的幽默和仿学术风格是否适合用于严肃的学术讨论，或者是否能被学术界接受和认可。

• 另一个可能的争议点在于[troelsSteegin] 提出的关于信息处理能力的观点，是否应被视为信息不对称问题中的核心要素，以及如何在具体模型中有效体现这一要素。

data.title: US Streetlights Are Turning Purple
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了街道LED路灯神秘变紫的现象及其潜在安全影响。近年来，美国及全球多地报告了路灯呈现紫色的情况。虽然看似无害，但这种色调变化可能影响司机和行人的视觉感知，从而构成安全隐患。

LED路灯通常通过蓝色LED和荧光涂层（磷）产生白光。当涂层剥落时，蓝色LED光暴露出来，因其带有紫色调，导致路灯变紫。可能的原因包括灯具内部过热、车辆震动或重力影响。

紫色光会影响人们对周围环境的感知，特别是在夜间驾驶或行走时，可能导致判断失误。因此，这一问题需要引起重视并加以解决。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• **技术故障观点**：  
  - bertm和padjo等人认为变色是由于LED中的磷层故障，可能是热循环失败或制造缺陷导致的。他们提到了具体的案例，如在凤凰城和爱尔兰发生的类似问题。
  - guicen进一步解释，许多人误以为紫色光是新设计，实际上是磷层损坏的结果。

  - cootsnuck认为一些城市选择廉价方案，导致使用蓝色光的街灯，这可能是为了节省成本，但影响了光质量。
  - fennecfoxy建议替换过热的LED灯，选择运行温度更低的方案。

• **光色对人的影响观点**：  
  - neilv抱怨高亮白光影响了睡眠和夜间行走体验，希望街灯能调整为更温暖的色温。
  - modeless则持不同意见，认为蓝白光在某些情况下能提高周边视觉，但聚焦时可能效果不佳，并指出对变化的批评总是存在的。

• **对文章和解决方案的批评观点**：  
  - joshstrange对相关文章的低努力程度表示不满，认为应该直接派人去检查而不是猜测，并批评文章中的科学解释不够具体。
  - davidmurdoch也认为制造商应负责更换有缺陷的灯，并以幽默方式表达对紫色灯的不满。

补充讨论：

September 27, 2023
5
min read
Streetlights Are Mysteriously Turning Purple. Here’s Why
Newly purple streetlights might seem innocuous, but they could affect driver and pedestrian safety
By
Karen Kwon
edited by
Sophie Bushwick
aire images/Getty Images
American cities and towns started switching their streetlights from sodium lamps to LEDs about 15 years ago, which changed the color of many nighttime roads from yellowish orange to bright white. But lately an odd new nocturnal color has been spotted across the nation—and the globe. Anecdotal reports of purple-looking streetlights have been popping up since early 2021 in states including
Florida
,
Utah
,
Texas
and
Massachusetts
, as well as in
Canada
and
Ireland
.
This phenomenon might seem weird but innocuous. After all, what
harm
could purple streetlights possibly do other than scare nearby residents as
Halloween approaches
? But it turns out that the hue of the light illuminating a roadway could affect how drivers and
pedestrians
perceive their surroundings as they make their way through the night. And that makes purple streetlights a potential safety hazard.
How do white LED streetlights work?
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
Updating streetlights to use light-emitting diodes makes sense. LEDs are one of
the most energy-efficient
lighting technologies that currently exist, according to the U.S. Department of Energy. They also tend to be more durable and longer-lasting than other types of lighting while producing light that is comparable or better in quality.
These diodes can emit light at a variety of wavelengths—but one color they do not produce naturally is white. So when you see white LEDs, such as those in streetlights, they are actually emanating some mixture of the colors red, green and blue (or red, yellow and blue), which together produce the appearance of white. There are two popular ways to create this illusion. One is to combine tiny LED lights that each emit red, green or blue into a single big device. The other is to use only blue LEDs but coat them with a type of fluorescent substance called phosphor. When the blue light from the diodes goes through this layer, the phosphor absorbs some of the blue wavelengths and spits out red and yellow ones. This results in a mixture of colors that, once again, appears white.
The second method gained popularity because it’s more energy-efficient than the first. LEDs that generate red and green light require more energy than those that emit blue, says Jakoah Brgoch, an associate professor of chemistry at the University of Houston. In addition to saving energy, the phosphor method also requires less electric circuitry than LEDs of three different colors do. This makes the streetlights less expensive, says John D. Bullough, a program director at the Light and Health Research Center, part of the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. This method does not work for all applications; televisions and color-changing lightbulbs, for instance, need to produce multiple colors of light. But to simply illuminate a street with a white light, manufacturers often opt for the cheaper and more efficient blue-LED-and-phosphor-coating combination.
But why are some streetlights suddenly turning purple?
The phosphor technique is sound, says Ram Seshadri, a materials science professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara. “Outside of my university, we’ve had LED lighting on the street for ... years, and there’s [been] no problem,” he adds.
And yet some streetlights have suddenly turned a jarring shade of purple. It is hard to determine the exact cause without dissecting one of the defective lights, but scientists have a hypothesis: bright purple light suggests the phosphor layer around the lights has been “delaminated”—peeled off—exposing the blue LED light underneath, Brgoch says. Although blue LED lights are, in principle, deep blue in color, they do naturally have a bit of a purple and violet tint, he explains.
It’s possible that the lamps themselves could be malfunctioning in various ways, but other malfunctions would produce different results. If the LED part were flawed, the light would go dark. And if the problem were the chemical degradation of the phosphor layer, the color would gradually turn from white to off-white, says postdoctoral researcher Shruti Hariyani at Texas A&M University, who studied phosphor materials with Brgoch for her doctoral degree.
As for the possible delamination of the lamps’ coating, it could be caused by anything: heat buildup inside the light fixture because of constant operation, vibrations from passing cars or even gravity tugging downward on the phosphor layer, according to Brgoch and Hariyani.

44301686.article_content:
So I was uh, downloading some linux isos, like usual. It was going slowly, so I opened up the
Trackers
tab in qBittorrent and saw the following:
Most of the trackers were totally dead.
Either the hosts were down or the domains werenât being used.
That got me thinking.
What if
I
picked up one of these dead domains?
How many clients would try to connect?
What are trackers for, anyways?
A
tracker
is a core component of the
BitTorrent protocol
. Trackers are the services that point you to other peers for the torrent. Without trackers, there would be no one to share the file with.
Obviously this represents a major source of centralization in the torrent protocol. If your trackers arenât maintained â or if they get forced offline by certain industry organizations â youâre out of luck.
We have an alternative, called
Mainline DHT
, which performs a more decentralized lookup of peers based on infohash alone. DHT isnât perfect, though. It relies on
bootstrap nodes
and is vulnerable to
Sybil attacks
. And in the example of my poorly-served torrent, DHT wasnât surfacing any peers, regardless.
Hosting a tracker
Looking through the list of trackers marked âhost not foundâ, I noticed
udp://open.demonii.si:1337/announce
was available.
I bought the domain through
Dynadot
(one of the few .si domain registrars), then spun up a
quick anonymous VPS
. I mapped the domain to the VPS, then set up
opentracker
, the most widely used and robust torrent tracker software.
Instructions for Ubuntu 24.04:
sudo
apt
install
gcc-14 g++-14 build-essential zlib1g-dev
sudo
update-alternatives
--install
/usr/bin/gcc gcc /usr/bin/gcc-14 14
sudo
update-alternatives
--install
/usr/bin/g++ g++ /usr/bin/g++-14 14
Follow the
readme
to compile, first the dependency
libowfat
(a GPL reimplementation of some of
dan bernstein
âs C libraries) and then opentracker itself.
cvs
-d
:pserver:cvs@cvs.fefe.de:/cvs
-z9
co libowfat
cd
libowfat
make
cd
..
git clone git://erdgeist.org/opentracker
cd
opentracker
make
Finally, a quick systemd unit file to daemonize this service:

Unit]

=
opentracker

network-online.target

=

simple

-p
1337

1337
\
-d
/var/lib/opentracker
-u
opentracker

=
on-failure

=
65536
[
Install]

=
multi-user.target

Before even starting opentracker, I saw a flood of traffic against UDP port 1337:
I then started the tracker. After about an hour, it peaked at about

data.title: Guidelines on how to be a scientific sleuth released
data.author: crescit_eundo
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了一个开源项目COSIG（**Collaborative Open Science Integrity Guides**），该项目旨在通过提供指南，帮助人们参与发表后的同行评审、科学文献的监督及科学 meta 分析。虽然审查科学文献的完整性通常需要特定领域的知识，但该项目通过专家编写的指南分享这些知识，让更多人能够参与。COSIG 包含28个指南，涵盖了从PubPeer评论最佳实践到图像查重等各类主题，并提供了单独和合并的PDF下载链接。项目还鼓励通过GitHub或邮件提交改进建议，并提供了贡献指南和行为准则。

### **Anyone can do post-publication peer review.**
### **Anyone can be a steward of the scientific literature.**
### **Anyone can do forensic metascience.**
### **Anyone can sleuth.**
However, investigating the integrity of the published scientific literature often requires domain-specific knowledge that not everyone will have. This open source project is a collection of guides written and maintained by publication integrity experts to distribute this domain-specific knowledge so that others can participate in post-publication peer review.
COSIG currently hosts 28 guides and was last updated on 13 June 2025. Guides can be downloaded as [individual PDFs](https://osf.io/2kdez/files/osfstorage). A combined PDF with all guides included can be downloaded [here](https://osf.io/ynb8j).
Suggestions to improve COSIG can be submitted by opening an issue on [COSIG's GitHub repo](https://github.com/cosig-pppr/cosig/issues) or by emailing [admin@cosig.net](mailto:admin@cosig.net). Before contributing, read COSIG's [Contributing](https://github.com/cosig-pppr/cosig/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/cosig-pppr/cosig/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) pages.

data.author: jsnider3

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对各种AI模型（特别是o3-pro）的使用体验和比较

不同观点：
• vessenes认为o3-pro在团队协作和会议安排等任务中表现优于o3和gemini/claude，尽管速度较慢，但在避免虚构信息方面更值得信任。他还提到，若能提升速度，o3-pro有可能被视为AGI。
• jes5199尚未尝试o3-pro，但基于o3的表现（如处理文件时的表现），表示有兴趣尝试o3-pro。
• b0a04gl指出，当o3价格下降80%时，许多人对其评价降低，但在实际任务运行中，o3在跨碎片化提示中保持状态的能力被低估了，尤其是在处理复杂任务时表现稳定且准确。
• snissn发现将问题分配给三个o3-pro实例并由另一个实例评估和综合，效果很好。
• highfrequency对o3-pro和deep research之间的区别感到困惑，因为两者响应时间相似且都基于o3模型。
• A_D_E_P_T认为，对于需要15-20分钟响应的工具，聊天格式并不理想，建议使用电子邮件格式更为合适。他还提到o3-pro的响应速度有所提升。
• franze使用Claude Code处理代码工作，并在遇到问题时使用o3-pro进行深度分析，效果显著。
• swyx对Arena的综合评价持有不同看法，认为其评比标准有待商榷。
• rotcev将o3-pro用作战略助理，而非编码模型，认为其延迟特性在处理影响生活的重要问题时是一种优势。
• metalrain从投资者的角度指出，质量和数量之间的“利润”取舍很重要，未来可能出现“向底线竞争”的趋势。
• boole1854详细比较了o3-pro、Gemini 2.5 Pro和Claude Opus 4在代码审查任务中的表现，发现每个模型都有其盲点，o3-pro尽管能发现一些其他模型忽略的问题，但也有虚构问题的倾向。
• starik36在法律专业邮件解析任务中未发现o3-pro比非pro版本有明显优势，甚至o1-preview表现更好。
• iLoveOncall认为长时间等待非常烦人，并发现非推理模型在90%的情况下能得到相同结果，因此选择使用非推理模型。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于o3-pro的响应速度和虚构问题。一些用户认为其深度和准确性值得等待，而另一些用户则对等待时间和虚构问题感到不满。
• 不同用户对模型的使用场景和需求各异，导致对各模型的评价有所不同。
• 用户在选择模型时，主要考虑的是模型的准确性、速度和特定任务需求。

data.title: Honda Conducts Successful Launch and Landing of Experimental Reusable Rocket
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 2025年6月17日，本田研发公司成功进行了自主研发的可重复使用火箭（长6.3米，直径85厘米，干重900公斤，湿重1,312公斤）的发射和着陆测试。火箭在达到300米高度后顺利着陆，验证了火箭在上升和下降过程中的飞行稳定性及着陆能力等关键技术。测试在日本北海道大樹町的本田设施进行，火箭达到了271.4米的飞行高度，并在预定着陆点37厘米范围内着陆，飞行持续56.6秒。本田自2024年起已在该地安全进行多次引擎点火和悬停测试，此次测试同样采取了严格的安全措施，设立了半径1公里的禁入区域。本田希望通过研发可重复使用火箭，实现其在太空技术领域的梦想，为人们日常生活创造更多价值，并应对未来卫星发射需求的增长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Honda小型火箭发射及其技术、竞争和实用性

不同观点：
• 3ds和jonplackett认为 Honda 应该在发射时提供视频记录，以增加透明度和记录这一重要时刻。

• _joel提到BPS.space的固体燃料推力矢量技术，并质疑其是否达到了Honda火箭的飞行高度，暗示对其他技术进展的关注。
• robszumski提供了Rocket Lab的Electron火箭的湿质量数据，以对比Honda火箭的规模，指出Honda火箭相对较小。
• whatever1质疑当今建造可重复使用火箭的容易程度，并将其可能原因归结为芯片计算能力的提升，能够解决更精细的控制问题。
• leesec认为Honda的火箭虽然成功发射并返回，但离实际应用还有很长的路要走，并指出比其他公司落后十年以上。
• cududa最初对首次发射成功表示 impressed，但质疑是否确实是首次发射，或者之前是否有未公开的失败尝试。
• walterbell从宏观角度指出，这次发射对日本来说是“一小步”，但对航天业竞争来说是“一大步”。
• ghxst祝贺工程师，并对.honda作为顶级域名表示惊讶和兴趣。
• adikulkarni11简单地称Honda火箭为“最可靠的火箭”，表达了对Honda技术可靠性的认可。
• pwarner从地缘政治角度出发，认为日本可能会对“一次性使用”的火箭应用感兴趣。

补充讨论：
• Honda火箭的技术细节，如推力矢量控制和其他技术进展的比较，是部分讨论的焦点。
• 火箭的实际应用和竞争态势，包括与其他公司的差距和地缘政治背景下的潜在需求，也被提及。
• 争议的焦点在于Honda火箭的实际成就和未来潜力，有人认为其离实用还有很长的路，有人则对其技术表示赞赏。

Jun 17, 2025
Topics
Honda Conducts Successful Launch and Landing Test of Experimental Reusable Rocket
TOKYO, Japan, June 17, 2025 â Honda R&D Co., Ltd., a research and development subsidiary of Honda Motor Co., Ltd., today conducted a launch and landing test of an experimental reusable rocket
*1
(6.3 m in length, 85 cm in diameter, 900 kg dry weight/1,312 kg wet weight) developed independently by Honda. The test was completed successfully, the first time Honda landed a rocket after reaching an altitude of 300 meters.
This test marked the first launch and landing test conducted by Honda with an aim to demonstrate key technologies essential for rocket reusability, such as flight stability during ascent and descent, as well as landing capability. Through this successful test, Honda achieved its intended rocket behaviors for the launch and landing (reaching an altitude of 271.4 m, and landing at 37cm of the target touchdown point, flight duration 56.6 sec), while obtaining data during the ascent and descent.
ï¼Overview of launch and landing test of a Honda reusable rocketï¼
ã»Purpose:Â Â Â Â  Establishment of key technologies necessary for a reusable rocket
ã»Location:Â Â Â Â  Honda facility in Taiki Town
*2
, Hiroo District, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan
ã»Date/Time:Â  June 17, 2025. Launch time: 16:15
Test being conducted in Taiki Town in Hokkaido, Japan(Photo taken in May, 2025)
Launch and landing test
*1 A reusable rocket, also known as a reusable launch vehicle (RLV), is a type of rocket that, unlike a conventional expendable launch vehicle (ELV), can be used repeatedly in a short period of time. A reusable rocket is launched in a vertical position, reaches an altitude of around 100 kilometers, and then lands back on earth while maintaining a vertical position.
*2 Taiki Town, located in southeastern Hokkaido, Japan, has been developing itself as a âspace townâ through the joint efforts of public and private sectors, and various aviation/space related tests are being conducted by a wide range of organizations including JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), businesses and universities.
ï¼Safety measures for Honda rocket testingï¼
Since 2024, Honda has been safely conducting engine combustion tests and hovering tests for its reusable rockets in Taiki Town in Hiroo District, Hokkaido, Japan. As with all previous tests, Honda conducted this launch and landing test while placing the highest priority on safety and with the understanding and cooperation of local authorities and residents.Â
Specific safety measures taken for this test
A restricted area with a 1-kilometer radius was established. During the test, access to the area was restricted through the installation of signs and gates, as well as the deployment of security personnel.
The restricted area was defined by calculating the potential area where the rocket could fall to earth in the event of a thrust cut-off and by adding a sufficient buffer zone (safe distance calculated based on the guidelines set forth by the Cabinet Office of the Government of Japan) that would cover the potential area where a blast wave, debris dispersion, or fireballs could impact in the event of an explosion within the potential fall area.
The experimental rocket was equipped with a safety system to prevent deviation from a pre-defined flight corridor, speed and attitude conditions, ensuring no impact beyond the restricted area.

44300102.article_summary: 2025年6月17日，本田研发公司成功进行了自主研发的可重复使用火箭（长6.3米，直径85厘米，干重900公斤，湿重1,312公斤）的发射和着陆测试。火箭在达到300米高度后顺利着陆，验证了火箭在上升和下降过程中的飞行稳定性及着陆能力等关键技术。测试在日本北海道大樹町的本田设施进行，火箭达到了271.4米的飞行高度，并在预定着陆点37厘米范围内着陆，飞行持续56.6秒。本田自2024年起已在该地安全进行多次引擎点火和悬停测试，此次测试同样采取了严格的安全措施，设立了半径1公里的禁入区域。本田希望通过研发可重复使用火箭，实现其在太空技术领域的梦想，为人们日常生活创造更多价值，并应对未来卫星发射需求的增长。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：西班牙电力系统大停电的原因及责任归属

不同观点：
• narag认为，此次大停电是由于政府控制的电力公司（REE）高层为了追求太阳能发电比例记录，不顾技术人员的意见，导致电网不稳定。他还指出，政府试图将责任归咎于缺乏足够的热电站，但故意不提核电，而核电是政府希望逐步淘汰的能源形式。私人企业要求公开CECOEL对话记录，部分日志泄露显示技术人员承认核电不足是导致波动原因。

• Rygian关注技术问题，强调“电压控制能力不足”是多年来的已知问题。REE在2019/2020年曾要求建立新的实时无功功率调度机制，因为西班牙仍然依赖基于电子邮件、电话甚至普通邮件的固定调度方式。2022年有一个成功的试点项目，但因成本过高，不符合欧盟的市场监管指令。

• cryptonector认为，停电是由于政策上“走钢丝”导致的，不仅仅是一个小小的计算错误，而是系统性问题。

• tux3指出，虽然报告已经提交，但尚未公开，提供了西班牙生态转型部的新闻链接。

• ZeroGravitas提到，几年前南澳大利亚大停电的根本原因是天然气发电厂谎报其可用性。

• Dr_Knows支持narag的观点，指出核电运营商在事发当天决定不供电。

• demarq质疑是否与俄罗斯有关，暗示可能有地缘政治因素影响。

补充讨论：
• 不同评论者对大停电原因有不同看法，部分关注技术问题，部分关注政策和管理问题。
• 核电的角色和其在停电中的影响是争议焦点之一，部分评论者认为政府故意不提核电问题。
• 也有评论者提到可能存在企业谎报发电能力的问题，类似于其他地区的停电事件。
• 总体来看，技术问题、政策决策、企业责任以及地缘政治因素都是讨论中的重要方面。

data.article_summary: 谷歌Gemini团队宣布扩展其Gemini 2.5模型系列。Gemini 2.5 Flash和Pro版本现已正式发布，具有高性能、成本和速度的优势。此外，他们还推出了Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite预览版，这是迄今为止最具成本效益和速度最快的2.5模型，具备更高的编码、数学、科学、推理等多方面能力，适用于高容量、低延迟的任务。开发者可以在Google AI Studio和Vertex AI中使用Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite预览版及稳定的Flash和Pro版本，并期待用户反馈。详细信息可参阅最新的Gemini技术报告。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• simonw和zhyder指出，Gemini 2.5 Flash模型的价格有所上升，尤其是输入和输出费用。zhyder认为，尽管2.0 Flash在某些用例中仍然是具有竞争力的选择，但2.5 Flash的提价让人感到遗憾。

Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro are now generally available, and we’re introducing 2.5 Flash-Lite, our most cost-efficient and fastest 2.5 model yet.
Tulsee Doshi
Senior Director, Product Management, on behalf of the Gemini team
Share

We designed Gemini 2.5 to be a family of hybrid reasoning models that provide amazing performance, while also being at the
Pareto Frontier
of cost and speed. Today, we’re taking the next step with our 2.5 Pro and Flash models by releasing them as stable and generally available. And we’re bringing you 2.5 Flash-Lite in preview — our most cost-efficient and fastest 2.5 model yet.
Making 2.5 Flash and 2.5 Pro generally available
Thanks to all of your feedback, today we’re releasing stable versions of 2.5 Flash and Pro, so you can build production applications with confidence.
Developers
like Spline and Rooms and
organizations
like Snap and SmartBear have already been using the latest versions in-production for the last few weeks.
Introducing Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
We’re also introducing a preview of the new Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, our most cost-efficient and fastest 2.5 model yet. You can start building with the preview version now, and we’re looking forward to your feedback.
2.5 Flash Lite has all-around higher quality than 2.0 Flash-Lite on coding, math, science, reasoning and multimodal benchmarks. It excels at high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks like translation and classification, with lower latency than 2.0 Flash-Lite and 2.0 Flash on a broad sample of prompts. It comes with the same capabilities that make Gemini 2.5 helpful, including the ability to turn thinking on at different budgets, connecting to tools like Google Search and code execution, multimodal input, and a 1 million-token context length.
See more details about our 2.5 family of models in the latest
Gemini technical report
.
The preview of Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite is now available in Google AI Studio and Vertex AI, alongside the stable versions of 2.5 Flash and Pro. Both 2.5 Flash and Pro are also accessible in the Gemini app. We’ve also brought custom versions of 2.5 Flash-Lite and Flash to Search.
We can’t wait to see what you continue to build with Gemini 2.5.

data.title: Voyager: Real-Time Splatting City-Scale 3D Gaussians on Your Phone
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为Voyager的系统，能够在移动设备上实时渲染城市规模的3D高斯溅射（3DGS）场景。由于移动设备资源有限，直接渲染此类场景存在困难。Voyager通过云端进行计算，但仅将用户视角中必要的高斯函数传输到客户端，以减少数据传输和延迟。云端采用异步细节层次搜索，客户端则通过查表式光栅化加速渲染。实验表明，Voyager在数据传输量上减少了超过100倍，速度提升最高达8.9倍，同时保持了相当的渲染质量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于图形渲染技术（尤其是“splatting”技术）在移动设备和云端的实现与优化

不同观点：
• reactordev：自2023年起在Faro Inc从事相关工作，并参与构建了该技术。他认为现代移动设备GPU性能强大，可以在几何着色器中实现查找光栅化（lookup rasterization），这是技术的核心。

• ge96：对最近频繁看到“splatting”技术表示疑惑，认为这是旧技术，不知为何重新流行。

• jauntywundrkind：询问是否已有部分渲染卸载到云端的实例，并分享了一种优化方案。他指出“splatting”本质上是一个搜索问题，可以卸载到云端处理。具体方法包括在云端进行异步细节层次搜索，以确定客户端所需的Gaussians，并在客户端通过基于查找表的光栅化加速渲染。

• modeless：询问是否有相关技术的 demo 演示，以更直观地理解该技术的实际应用。

补充讨论：
• reactordev 强调了现代移动设备GPU的性能进步，使得复杂渲染操作可以在本地设备上高效完成。
• ge96 对“splatting”技术重新受到关注表示不解，暗示该技术可能已经过时或被取代。
• jauntywundrkind 提出了云端与客户端协作的优化方案，强调了云端处理搜索问题和客户端加速渲染的结合。
• modeless 关注实际演示，希望通过demo更深入理解该技术的实际效果。

争议焦点：
• “splatting”技术是否为过时的技术，以及其重新受到关注的原因。

Abstract:
3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is an emerging technique for photorealistic 3D scene rendering. However, rendering city-scale 3DGS scenes on mobile devices, e.g., your smartphones, remains a significant challenge due to the limited resources on mobile devices. A natural solution is to offload computation to the cloud; however, naively streaming rendered frames from the cloud to the client introduces high latency and requires bandwidth far beyond the capacity of current wireless networks.
In this paper, we propose an effective solution to enable city-scale 3DGS rendering on mobile devices. Our key insight is that, under normal user motion, the number of newly visible Gaussians per second remains roughly constant. Leveraging this, we stream only the necessary Gaussians to the client. Specifically, on the cloud side, we propose asynchronous level-of-detail search to identify the necessary Gaussians for the client. On the client side, we accelerate rendering via a lookup table-based rasterization. Combined with holistic runtime optimizations, our system can deliver low-latency, city-scale 3DGS rendering on mobile devices. Compared to existing solutions, Voyager achieves over 100$\times$ reduction on data transfer and up to 8.9$\times$ speedup while retaining comparable rendering quality.

44298724.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为Voyager的系统，能够在移动设备上实时渲染城市规模的3D高斯溅射（3DGS）场景。由于移动设备资源有限，直接渲染此类场景存在困难。Voyager通过云端进行计算，但仅将用户视角中必要的高斯函数传输到客户端，以减少数据传输和延迟。云端采用异步细节层次搜索，客户端则通过查表式光栅化加速渲染。实验表明，Voyager在数据传输量上减少了超过100倍，速度提升最高达8.9倍，同时保持了相当的渲染质量。

主要讨论点：关于图形渲染技术（尤其是“splatting”技术）在移动设备和云端的实现与优化

• reactordev：自2023年起在Faro Inc从事相关工作，并参与构建了该技术。他认为现代移动设备GPU性能强大，可以在几何着色器中实现查找光栅化（lookup rasterization），这是技术的核心。

data.title: Cmapv2: A high performance, concurrent map
data.author: sirgallo
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Go语言中的一个并发哈希数组映射前缀树（concurrent hash array mapped trie）实现，名为cmapv2。该项目提供了安装和使用指南，用户可以通过`go get`命令将其集成到自己的Go项目中。cmapv2支持常规的键值对插入、获取和删除操作，并且可以初始化分片的并发地图（sharded c map）以提高性能。项目包含测试代码和性能分析指南，用户可以通过运行测试命令和性能分析工具来评估其表现。该项目基于MIT许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对 `cmapv2` 代码库的安全性、性能及其与其它类似工具的比较存在不同看法。

不同观点：
• [kiitos] 认为 `cmapv2` 代码库存在严重问题，指出代码中广泛存在对 "atomic" 读取 `unsafe.Pointer` 值的误用，导致数据竞争问题。他认为该代码库不安全，不能使用，并通过引用具体代码 [1] 来支持其论点。

• [sirgallo] 作为 `cmapv2` 的维护者，强调该库的性能优势，指出其在性能上与 Go 的 `sync.Map` 相比具有竞争力，甚至在某些工作负载下表现更优。他特别提到 `cmapv2` 是无锁且线程安全的，依赖于原子操作，并且原生支持分片（sharding）。他还提供了性能数据（如在特定条件下每秒读写操作次数）来证明其观点。

• [gttalbot] 提出了 `cmapv2` 与 "swisstables" 的对比问题，暗示对 `cmapv2` 是否能与这种数据结构相媲美存在疑问。虽然没有详细展开，但这个问题暗示了对 `cmapv2` 性能和实用性的潜在挑战。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点集中在 `cmapv2` 的安全性和性能上。`kiitos` 关注代码的安全性和正确性，而 `sirgallo` 则侧重于性能优势和实现细节。
• `gttalbot` 的评论引入了与 "swisstables" 的比较，这可能是一个值得进一步讨论的方向，尤其是在性能和数据结构设计方面。

总体来看，讨论的核心围绕着 `cmapv2` 的代码安全性、性能表现以及与其他技术方案的可比性。

data.title: CPU-Based Layout Design for Picker-to-Parts Pallet Warehouses
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种受CPU架构启发的仓储布局设计，用于优化“拣货到零件”的托盘仓库效率。该设计将仓库空间划分为性能区（P）、效率区（E）和共享区（S），并通过离散事件模拟与传统布局（如矩形和Flying-V布局）进行对比。结果显示，该设计显著提高了吞吐量并减少了人工需求。文章由Timo Looms和Lin Xie撰写，发表于arXiv，共8页，包含6个图表，适用于多智能体系统领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：仓库管理系统的演变和优化

不同观点：
• ribfeasty 分享了实际运营全国最大DVD租赁业务的经历，描述了仓库管理从人工操作到数据库自动化调配的演变过程。他提到早期的系统通过扫描DVD并自动分配到仓库空位，从而优化了新发行和归还DVD的处理流程，最终实现了仓库的高效运作。例子包括利用早期Dell AXIMs设备和无线技术（wifi）来实现实时管理和调配，并提到为了避免拥堵，系统会动态调整仓库内的库存布局。

• kens 则从理论角度出发，讨论了模拟仓库中基于"性能"和"效率"分区的概念，类似于CPU中性能核心和效率核心的分工。他提到模拟结果显示这种分区方法有效，但指出论文未深入探讨其原因。这表明他更关注理论模型和其背后的原理，而非实际操作细节。

补充讨论：
• ribfeasty 更强调实际操作经验和早期技术应用，提供了具体的设备（Dell AXIMs、红激光扫描器、wifi）和操作细节（如库存动态调整、行走通道的优化），展示了技术在实际业务中的应用和效果。

• kens 则侧重于理论模拟和系统架构设计，关注的是如何通过分区策略提升仓库整体效率，并对模拟结果的理论基础提出质疑，希望进一步探讨其背后的原理。

争议焦点：
• 实际操作经验与理论模型之间的差异。ribfeasty 提供了丰富的实际案例，而 kens 则更注重理论框架和其解释力，两者反映了实践与理论的不同侧重点。

Abstract:
Picker-to-parts pallet warehouses often face inefficiencies due to conventional layouts causing excessive travel distances and high labor requirements. This study introduces a novel layout design inspired by CPU architecture, partitioning warehouse space into specialized zones, namely Performance (P), Efficiency (E), and Shared (S). Discrete-event simulation is used to evaluate this design against traditional rectangular (random and ABC storage) and Flying-V layouts. Results demonstrate significant improvements in throughput time and reduced labor requirements, highlighting the potential for CPU-based layouts in optimizing warehouse operations.

• ribfeasty 更强调实际操作经验和早期技术应用，提供了具体的设备（Dell AXIMs、红激光扫描器、wifi）和操作细节（如库存动态调整、行走通道的优化），展示了技术在实际业务中的应用和效果。

• kens 则侧重于理论模拟和系统架构设计，关注的是如何通过分区策略提升仓库整体效率，并对模拟结果的理论基础提出质疑，希望进一步探讨其背后的原理。

争议焦点：
• 实际操作经验与理论模型之间的差异。ribfeasty 提供了丰富的实际案例，而 kens 则更注重理论框架和其解释力，两者反映了实践与理论的不同侧重点。

data.title: Now might be the best time to learn software development
data.author: nathanfig
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具是否会取代软件开发人员，以及这些工具对开发人员工作的实际影响。

不同观点：
• **psunavy03**: 通过幽默的方式暗示，即使有像COBOL这样的工具让非技术人员写代码，技术债务和代码质量问题依然存在，最终还是需要专业开发人员来清理。
• **rossdavidh**: 认为尽管AI工具出现，组织仍不应该解雇开发人员。指出大部分开发人员的时间都花在了不那么有实际产出的项目上，且远程工作的趋势可能导致低工资地区的竞争。
• **michaelteter**: 认为AI工具虽然可能导致企业做出不利于开发人员的决策，但同时也为有创造力的开发人员提供了机会，可以通过独立项目创造收入并可能被企业收购。
• **nathanfig**: 提出反叙事，反对对软件开发人员价值的悲观看法，鼓励分享个人观点和经验。
• **dehrmann**: 关注AI能力的上限以及对更多软件的需求量，提出Jevons悖论中的需求弹性问题，暗示AI工具可能不会无限提升效率。
• **temporallobe**: 认为低代码或无代码解决方案一直以来都导致非技术人员制造问题，最终还是需要工程师来解决，这样的情况已经为一些工程师创造了 lucrative 职业机会。
• **abalashov**: 部分同意rossdavidh的观点，但认为编码能力的价值已经通过外包浪潮体现，未来更看重的是领域专业知识和跨技术与非技术利益相关者之间的沟通能力。
• **karczex**: 通过类比Fortran，暗示即使有新工具让非技术人员写代码，专业开发人员的需求依然存在。
• **yodsanklai**: 提到目前使用AI工具生成代码后仍需要人工审查和重写，暗示AI工具尚不能完全取代人类开发人员。
• **waffletower**: 提到一个鼓舞人心的资源链接，暗示在AI工具时代仍需要开发人员具备深入的技术知识和创造力。
• **prisenco**: 提到在Upwork上已经有非技术人员使用低代码工具制造问题并需要专业开发人员帮助解决的案例。
• **SeanDav**: 纠正关于“ChadGPT”的拼写错误，指出实际应该是ChatGPT。
• **mirkodrummer**: 对LLMs能代替许多人的工作的说法表示怀疑，认为目前AI工具仅能自动化部分繁琐的工作，尚不能取代多个同事的工作。
• **fuzztester**: 通过幽默方式回应使用AI工具的场景，暗示对过度宣传AI工具能力的反感。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI工具是否能真正取代开发人员，尤其是在低代码/无代码工具的历史背景下，许多评论者认为最终还是需要专业开发人员来解决复杂问题。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是AI工具对开发人员工作效率的实际影响，部分评论者认为这些工具更多是辅助作用，而非完全取代。
• 对AI工具的过度宣传和不切实际的期望也是讨论的一个重要方面，许多评论者对此持怀疑态度。

data.title: Celebrated pianist and writer Alfred Brendel dies aged 94
data.author: mykowebhn
data.article_summary: 阿尔弗雷德·布伦德尔（Alfred Brendel），著名钢琴家兼作家，于2025年6月17日在伦敦去世，享年94岁。他出生于摩拉维亚，童年在克罗地亚和奥地利度过，16岁后自学成才。1949年，他获得布索尼比赛第四名，开启了演奏生涯。布伦德尔以演绎贝多芬作品闻名，是首位录制贝多芬全部钢琴作品的钢琴家，同时推动了海顿、舒伯特和勋伯格等人作品的复兴。他移居伦敦后，于1971年定居汉普斯特德，育有三个孩子。2008年在维也纳举行最后一场公开音乐会，之后继续出版诗歌和散文，并授课。他被誉为“音乐家的音乐家”和“钢琴家的导师”，学生包括保罗·刘易斯和伊莫金·库珀等。他获得了23个荣誉学位和多项国际大奖，其逝世是音乐界的巨大损失。

44301246.article_content:
Alfred Brendel in 2010.
Photograph: unknown/Sophia Evans
View image in fullscreen
Alfred Brendel in 2010.
Photograph: unknown/Sophia Evans
Classical music
Celebrated pianist and writer Alfred Brendel dies aged 94
Widely regarded as the ‘musicians’ musician’ Brendel was the first pianist to record all of Beethoven’s piano works during a much-garlanded career spanning 60 years
Imogen Tilden
Tue 17 Jun 2025 12.24 EDT
Last modified on Tue 17 Jun 2025 12.47 EDT
Share
The celebrated pianist and author
Alfred Brendel
has died aged 94 at his home in London.
The musician was born on 5 January 1931 in Moravia (now part of the Czech Republic) and spent his childhood mainly in Croatia and Austria. “I was not a child prodigy or eastern European or Jewish as far as I know,”
he told interviewers
. “I’m not a good sight reader, I don’t have a phenomenal memory and I didn’t come from a musical family, an artistic family or an intellectual family. I had loving parents, but I had to find things out for myself.”
He studied piano and composition until he was 16,
thereafter he was largely self-taught
. Aged 17 he gave his first public recital in Graz with works by Bach, Brahms and Liszt on the programme, one of the encores was his own composition – a sonata with a double fugue. The teenage Brendel was also an author and an exhibited painter, but in 1949 he won fourth prize in the prestigious Busoni competition, which launched his career as a performing musician.
His concert and recording career lasted more than 60 years with performances at the world’s most important musical centres and festivals alongside the leading orchestras and conductors. He became particularly associated with the music of Beethoven, and made the first complete recording of the composer’s entire piano music. He took a prominent role in highlighting Haydn’s importance as a composer
,
in establishing
Schubert’s Sonatas and Schoenberg’s Concerto in the repertoire, and rekindling interest in Liszt’s piano music. He moved to London in 1971, and made his home in Hampstead, his second marriage brought three children (his son,
Adrian is an acclaimed cellist
, his daughter by his first,
Doris, is a pop and rock singer
). His final public
concert was in Vienna in 2008
but in the succeeding years he published poetry and essays, lectured and continued to teach and give masterclasses.
View image in fullscreen
Inspirational and uncompromising: Alfred Brendel.
Photograph: Benjamin Ealovega
“I don’t feel guilty about being ‘intellectual’ if that means thinking about the structure and character and humour in a piece of music,”
he told the Guardian in 2010
on the occasion of receiving Gramophone magazine’s Lifetime Achievement award. “But I’m not talking about dry analysis, which is relatively easy if you know how. I do the opposite. I familiarise myself with a piece and wait for it to tell me what it’s about, and what makes it a masterpiece. That’s what fascinates.”
Widely regarded by colleagues as the “musicians’ musician” as well as the “pianists’ mentor”: Brendel’s pupils include Paul Lewis, Imogen Cooper, Kit Armstrong and Till Fellner and he devoted a significant part of his time to sharing his experiences as a musician with younger artists.
“Alfred Brendel was my guide, mentor and an endless source of inspiration for more than 30 years, and his passing is an enormous loss not only for music, but on a personal level for those of us who were fortunate enough to be guided and touched by his wisdom and insight, of which he gave so generously and selflessly,” said Lewis. “[He] was unique in the pantheon of great pianists – inspirational and uncompromising, with a formidable knowledge of literature and art as well as of music. His playing was intense and visionary, his teaching no less so – but dry humour was never far,” added Cooper.
Brendel received 23 honorary degrees from universities including Weimar, Cambridge, Oxford, Yale and The Juilliard School, the Honorary Vice-Presidency of the Royal Academy of Music and a number of prestigious awards such as honorary membership in the Vienna Philharmonic, the Sonning and Siemens prizes and the Praemium Imperiale in Japan.

data.title: Tesla Robotaxi launch is a dangerous game of smoke and mirrors
data.author: apayan
data.article_summary: Tesla's upcoming Robotaxi launch in Austin, Texas, appears to be more of a strategic illusion rather than a true advancement in autonomous driving technology. CEO Elon Musk has a history of overpromising and missing deadlines regarding full self-driving capabilities. Although he now claims Tesla has "solved" self-driving with the Robotaxi launch, this involves geofencing, teleoperation, and limited routes, differing significantly from previous promises of unsupervised, widespread autonomy. The launch seems aimed at maintaining the perception that Tesla leads in autonomous driving, especially as competitors like Waymo expand their services. Despite Musk's assurances of being "paranoid" about safety, the rushed nature of the launch and reliance on teleoperation raise questions about its true autonomy and scalability.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tesla的自动驾驶技术（FSD）及其未来前景，特别是与Waymo的对比，以及Tesla的整体生存能力。

不同观点：
• **[看空Tesla的观点]** [blindriver] 和 [turnsout] 对Tesla持悲观态度。他们认为Tesla的销售下滑，且FSD技术不成熟，无法与Waymo竞争。他们特别指出，Tesla的机器人出租车计划是绝望中的挣扎，可能导致事故，并进一步损害品牌。同时，他们提到Elon Musk的政治立场和决策对品牌的负面影响。
  
• **[中立但批评FSD局限性的观点]** [jjcm] 拥有两辆Tesla，并且经常使用FSD。虽然他认为FSD在天气良好时表现出色，但在动态环境下的稳定性不足。相比之下，他认为Waymo的方法更优，因为单靠视觉技术不足以实现完全自动驾驶。

• **[支持Waymo的观点]** [stingrae] 强调Waymo在关键脱离里程数（Critical Disengagement）上的优势，指出Waymo在实际运行中的表现远超Tesla，预示可能发生比以往自动驾驶事故更严重的事件。

• **[支持Tesla的观点]** [leesec] 对Tesla的FSD技术持乐观态度，认为其表现良好，且在实际驾驶中表现出色。他提到一位Uber司机在使用FSD技术时无需人工干预驾驶了16,000英里。

• **[Tesla数据优势的观点]** [iw7tdb2kqo9] 认为Tesla在实际道路测试数据上拥有优势，尽管Waymo目前在技术上领先，但Tesla有潜力通过大量数据提升其自动驾驶技术。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Tesla FSD技术是否能够与Waymo竞争，特别是在实际应用中的安全性和可靠性。批评者认为Tesla的视觉技术不足以应对复杂环境，而支持者则认为Tesla拥有更多的实际驾驶数据，未来有机会改善。
  
• **具体例子**：评论中提到了具体的技术对比，如FSD在天气良好时的表现优于人类驾驶，但在恶劣天气下表现不佳；以及Waymo在关键脱离里程数上的显著优势。

• **对Tesla品牌的影响**：有评论指出Tesla的品牌形象因Elon Musk的政治立场和机器人出租车计划而受损，这可能影响其市场表现和消费者信心。

44300727.article_content:
Tesla
Tesla Robotaxi launch is a dangerous game of smoke and mirrors
Fred Lambert
| Jun 16 2025 - 5:55 am PT
324 Comments
Tesla’s upcoming Robotaxi launch in Austin, Texas, is increasingly looking like a game of smoke and mirrors, and a dangerous one at that.
CEO Elon Musk claims Tesla is being “paranoid with safety”, but it is taking risks for the purpose of optics.
It’s all about optics
Musk has been wrong about self-driving for years. His track record is marked by missed deadlines and broken promises.
He said:
Advertisement - scroll for more content
“Our goal is, and I feel pretty good about this goal, that we’ll be able to do a demonstration drive of full autonomy all the way from LA to New York, from home in LA to let’s say dropping you off in Times Square in New York, and then having the car go park itself, by the end of next year. Without the need for a single touch, including the charger.”
That was in 2016, and therefore, he claimed it would happen by the end of 2017. Today, in 2025, Tesla is still not capable of doing that.
Musk has claimed that Tesla would achieve unsupervised self-driving every year for the last decade. It has become a running gag
, with many YouTube videos featuring his predictions and
a Wikipedia page
tr
acking his missed deadlines.
Famously, the predictions are about Tesla achieving self-driving “by the end of the year” or “next year.”
This time, Musk has set a clear deadline of “June” for Tesla to launch its robotaxi service.
With Waymo pulling ahead in the autonomous driving race, now operating in four cities, providing over 200,000 paid rides per week, and soon expanding with 2,000 more vehicles, Musk needs a win to maintain the illusion he has been pushing for a while: that Tesla is the leader in autonomous driving.
He recently claimed about Tesla’s self-driving technology:
No one is even close. There’s really not a close second. We felt like it was a bit of an iPhone moment — you either get it or you don’t, and there’s a massive gap.
This is becoming increasingly difficult to claim amid Waymo’s expansion. Still, Musk believes that the robotaxi launch in Austin will help maintain the illusion, even though Waymo has already been operating like Tesla’s plans in Austin for years in other cities and for months in Austin itself.
Moving of the Goal Post
We have often described what Tesla is doing in Austin with its planned “robotaxi” launch as
a moving of the goalpost
.
For years, Tesla has promised unsupervised self-driving in all its vehicles built since 2016. Musk explicitly said that customers who bought Tesla’s Full Self-Driving package would be able to “go to sleep” at the wheel of their vehicles and wake up in another city.
Now, Musk is claiming that Tesla has “solved” self-driving with its “robotaxi” launch, but it is vastly different from prior promises.
Tesla plans to operate its own small internal fleet of vehicles with dedicated software optimized for a geo-fenced area of Austin and supported by “
plenty of teleoperation
.” This is a night-and-day difference compared to deploying unsupervised self-driving in customer vehicles, as promised since 2016.
Musk himself is on
record
saying, “If you need a geofence area, you don’t have real self-driving.”
Now, Musk is on record saying that Tesla will only launch the service in a limited area in Austin and even avoid certain intersections that Tesla is not sure it can handle:
We will geo‑fence it. It’s not going to take intersections unless we are highly confident it’s going to do well with that intersection. Or it will just take a route around that intersection.
In addition to geofencing, Tesla is also utilizing teleoperation to control vehicles with human operators remotely.
We reported last year when
Tesla started building a “teleoperation team.”
Despite Tesla originally planning to launch the robotaxi service on June 12, and now “tentatively” on June 22, the automaker posted a new job listing days ago for engineers to help build a low-latency teleoperation system to operate its “self-driving” cars and robots.
The use of geofencing and teleoperation results in Tesla having the same limitations as Waymo, which Musk claimed means it’s “not real self-driving and not scalable to the customer fleet as promised by Tesla for years.
‘Paranoid’ about Safety
Musk claims that Tesla is being “super paranoid” about safety, but you have to take his word for it.
We have pointed it out before, but it’s worth repeating: Waymo tested its self-driving vehicles in Austin for six months with safety drivers and then for another six months without safety drivers before launching its autonomous ride-hailing service in the city.
As for Tesla, it tested its vehicles with safety drivers throughout Austin for a few months. Then, Musk announced in late May, only weeks before the planned launch, that
it had started testing without safety drivers
.
Despite many people being on the lookout for these driverless Tesla Robotaxis,

44300727.article_summary: Tesla's upcoming Robotaxi launch in Austin, Texas, appears to be more of a strategic illusion rather than a true advancement in autonomous driving technology. CEO Elon Musk has a history of overpromising and missing deadlines regarding full self-driving capabilities. Although he now claims Tesla has "solved" self-driving with the Robotaxi launch, this involves geofencing, teleoperation, and limited routes, differing significantly from previous promises of unsupervised, widespread autonomy. The launch seems aimed at maintaining the perception that Tesla leads in autonomous driving, especially as competitors like Waymo expand their services. Despite Musk's assurances of being "paranoid" about safety, the rushed nature of the launch and reliance on teleoperation raise questions about its true autonomy and scalability.

• **[支持Waymo的观点]** [stingrae] 强调Waymo在关键脱离里程数（Critical Disengagement）上的优势，指出Waymo在实际运行中的表现远超Tesla，预示可能发生比以往自动驾驶事故更严重的事件。

• **[Tesla数据优势的观点]** [iw7tdb2kqo9] 认为Tesla在实际道路测试数据上拥有优势，尽管Waymo目前在技术上领先，但Tesla有潜力通过大量数据提升其自动驾驶技术。

data.title: Windows 10 EOL
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲述了作者因微软停止支持Windows 10以及对硬件的任意淘汰政策，不得不为家庭中的多台电脑进行升级或系统更换的经历。作者管理着多台设备，包括笔记本电脑、台式机和NUC。由于Windows 11的硬件要求，作者的妻子和儿子的电脑需要进行不同的处理，部分设备被替换为新硬件。作者为自己选择了一台高配置的Ryzen 9900x系统，并为其他设备安装了Linux或Windows 11。在更换系统过程中，作者遇到了一些问题，如操作系统语言、Wi-Fi兼容性和软件迁移等，但总体上对新硬件的质量感到满意。最终，作者成功地完成了所有设备的升级和系统安装。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows 11的硬件限制及其引发的电子废物问题

不同观点：
• **反对微软硬件限制的观点**：
  - [ralferoo] 批评微软制造不必要的电子废物，认为作为软件公司应尽可能支持更多硬件，而不是强迫用户购买新设备。
  - [vondur] 以实际工作经验为例，指出大学中大量计算机因无法运行支持版本的Windows而被替换，可能导致电子废物问题。
  - [neepi] 表示不愿因Windows 11的限制而丢弃高性能硬件（如Z440工作站），并选择使用Windows 10 LTSC版本延长设备寿命。
  - [oneZergArmy] 提到其两台笔记本电脑因无法安装Linux而面临淘汰，批评厂商不开放BIOS。
  
• **支持或接受微软决定的观点**：
  - [CursedSilicon] 解释微软基于硬件对Meltdown和Spectre漏洞的缓解能力做出限制，认为此决定并非 arbitrary（武断）。
  - [v9v] 认为即使微软停止支持Windows 10，系统并不会立刻无法使用，质疑人们夸大电子废物问题。
  - [EvanAnderson] 分享通过命令行绕过限制，在“不支持”的PC上安装Windows 11，认为可以延长设备使用寿命。

• **其他系统替代方案的观点**：
  - [caycep] 建议推广Debian或其衍生版（如PopOS），并提到其办公室通过绕过Win11安装检查继续使用旧设备。
  - [riobard] 呼吁Linux社区团结，吸引Windows 10用户转向Linux系统。
  - [DanAtC] 提到Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC支持到2032年，提供了一种延长使用Windows系统的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• **市场数据引用**：
  - [personalityson] 引用数据指出53%的Windows PC仍在使用不同版本的Windows 10，显示Windows 11普及率有限。
  
• **硬件兼容性问题**：
  - [Lammy] 描述因主板限制只能使用Windows 10 v1909，但认为没有更新的体验也不错，甚至更稳定。
  
• **对Windows功能的批评**：
  - [ReptileMan] 批评Windows 11/10相较Windows 7没有显著改进，特别指出Windows商店和搜索功能的不足，唯一亮点是WSL（Windows Subsystem for Linux）。

• **关于W10许可证销售的疑问**：
  - [throw_m239339] 询问是否能在翻新市场继续销售Windows 10许可证，因许多硬件无法满足Windows 11的图形卡要求。

争议焦点：微软是否应基于硬件限制强制用户升级到Windows 11，以及此举对电子废物问题的影响。

Windows 10 EOL
June 17th, 2025
(permalink)
So Microsoft decided to produce tons of e-waste for no obvious reason. There's a lot of capable hardware out there, and it would be of software company's interest to support as much hardware as possible. Instead, they made some arbitrary reason to deprecate "old" hardware. At the same time they also turned all of windows VR headsets into garbage. We'll have to wait for the open source implementations to catch up for any hope of them being usable again. From what I read, there's some certificate issues in the way there, but maybe there's some hope. We'll see.
I've found myself in a situation where I'm the admin for 5 laptops, 3 desktop systems and 2 NUCs within the family. Except for the NUCs, all of which were running windows 10. (One NUC is running Debian, the other already had win11).
Son's PC was new enough that it just needed a BIOS tweak and it upgraded to windows 11.
Wife's PC was too old for windows 11, and had some motherboard damage (using network through an USB dongle, stuff like that), so I just ordered a new relatively cheap desktop PC. Not a beast, but more than good enough to run games. This came from
verkkokauppa.com
, of all places. I did shop around and they happened to have a no-brand prebuilt with decent specs. I was positively surprised by the build quality, cable management and everything.
My PC was technically new enough for win11, but I didn't feel comfortable not having a working system for a while, so after long, long contemplation decided to buy a new PC for myself as well. And if I was getting a new PC, it would have to be an upgrade. My old system has ryzen7 2700 with 8 cores. So the base had to be "more than 8 cores". I compared what's available at the moment and both Intel and AMD have "more than 8 cores" consumer systems at comparable prices and comparable performance. Intel's solution has big and little cores while AMD's solution has all big cores.
I contemplated the pros and cons of each from a developer perspective - on one hand it would be interesting to test with a system that has different sized cores... and on the other hand, I'd probably have fewer issues overall with a "all cores are the same" system. So in the end I went with the Ryzen 9900x 12 core system. I also opted for 64 gigs of memory, in hopes that I wouldn't need to upgrade for several years. Maybe a GPU update at some point.
This came from
Takomo
, a small local company that builds high end gaming PCs. I was positively surprised about them at almost every step. The web store has a computer builder which gives information about every part you choose. They contacted me afterwards offering advice if I was building a gaming PC (likely to suggest more cooling and beefier GPU). The computer arrived on time, extremely well packaged, with some clearly labelled boxes for spare parts, PSU cables and candy. The build quality looks top notch, and the only little glitch was that the OS was in Finnish. Not that reinstalling the OS was a big deal compared to all the migration setup I had to do.
Including Photoshop CS5. Adobe very kindly has installer for it in your account if you registered it back whenever, even though the license servers no longer exist. So I'm still able to use my legal copy of Photoshop CS5. I did leave some software behind on purpose, including UltraEdit.
I also did end up installing win11 on my old system, with the plan being to use it as a dedicated audio production system, in hopes that it would lead to fewer glitches compared to the other system which will have
all the software
.. on win10 I had random several-millisecond kernel level pauses, which isn't great when recording audio.
Which then brings us to the laptops.
For my mother in law, her laptop that's used mainly to pay bills and such, was both too old for win11 and a piece of crap to begin with, so I ordered a refurbished ThinkPad as a replacement. That came with win11... in German. After jumping through the hoops to get the system running and license locked to my account, I reinstalled the system.
For the rest of the laptops, I installed Linux. Ubuntu, to be precise, selected because it's the largest distro out there, in hopes that it would lead to fewest issues. I did not opt for Linux for my mother in law for obvious reasons - if she had issues using her net bank, using windows would make it the bank's problem, not mine.
Most of the laptops took Linux just fine. In one case I had to buy a new, Linux-compatible WIFI m.2 thingy. What do they call them anyway? Sticks? In another case I fought with the system to get hyperthreading working (the CPU stats had ht flag, but smt didn't work),
